name: Taurasi
terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
keyfacts: Under DOCG rules Taurasi must be aged at least 3 years before release, with at least 1 year in wood, and Riserva at least 4 years.
Up to 15% of other non-aromatic red grapes approved for Avellino province may be blended with the Aglianico.
The Aglianico vineyards sit on hills between about ⟦elev|1,300 and 2,300 feet|400 and 700 m⟧, on soils rich in clay and limestone with volcanic ash deposits in parts of the zone.

notes: It is deep ruby, turning garnet and then orange-tinged with age.
It is dry, full and balanced, with a long finish.

blurb.text: A red wine from Avellino province in Campania, based principally on Aglianico and grown on hillside vineyards. It became a DOC in 1970 and a DOCG in 1993.
